title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Grothendieck's combinatorial formalism for 'cartes' (maps on surfaces), written in terms of 'repères' (flags). A repère is a triangle of the barycentric subdivision with vertices s (type 0, vertex), ã (type 1, edge-centre) and f̃ (type ∞, face-centre). The reflections τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞ (written σ_i on this page) act on flags. Each τ_i changes the type-i vertex of a flag and fixes the other two. The rotations are ρ_∞=τ_1τ_0, ρ_1=τ_0τ_∞ and ρ_0=τ_∞τ_1. Their product is 1, and ρ_1^2=1 because τ_0 and τ_∞ commute.

(1) Duality. The dual map Č is defined combinatorially. It has the same underlying surface, triangulated by the same flags, but the roles of the type-0 and type-∞ vertices are exchanged. So vertices of C become faces of Č and conversely, and edges correspond bijectively, preserving incidence. A common flag r, read as a flag of Č instead of C, induces the opposite orientation. Hence it gives opposite orientations on edges and opposite senses of rotation around vertices. In group terms, duality is the automorphism of the cartographic group that swaps τ_0 and τ_∞.

(2) Orientation. A map X is oriented when its surface is oriented. Equivalently, the flag set R(X) is split into two complementary parts R^+ ⊔ R^- such that each σ_i sends R^+ into R^-, hence onto it. It follows that the σ_i exchange R^+ and R^-, while the ρ_i preserve each part. So R^+(X) is a set with an action of the oriented cartographic group
  G_2^+ = <ρ_0, ρ_1, ρ_∞ | ρ_1^2 = 1, ρ_0ρ_1ρ_∞ = 1> ≅ Z/2 * Z,
the index-2 subgroup of G_2 = <τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞ | τ_i^2 = 1, (τ_0τ_∞)^2 = 1>.

(3) Main statement (8). X ↦ R^+(X) is an equivalence between oriented maps and finite G_2^+-sets. A final NB announces a non-trivial notion of morphism of maps.

This serves the Teichmüller / dessins d'enfants programme. Finite G_2^+-sets correspond to finite-index subgroups of the oriented cartographic group, which is a quotient of π_1 of P^1 minus {0, 1, ∞}. The equivalence is one link in the chain dessins ↔ Belyi pairs ↔ maps on which the Galois group Gal(Q̄/Q) acts.
errors: Line (7) as transcribed (and apparently as written) reads σ_i(R^+)=R^+, σ_i(R^-)=R^-. The intended statement, implied by (6 bis), is σ_i(R^+)=R^- and σ_i(R^-)=R^+. This is either a slip of the pen or a transcription error; only (7 bis), for the ρ_i, preserves R^±.

For the equivalence (8) to be exact, 'carte' must include degenerate cases. Arbitrary finite G_2^+-sets can have fixed points of ρ_1 (half-edges / free edges) or of ρ_0 and ρ_∞. These do not arise from honest triangulated closed surfaces with free flag actions. Presumably the earlier definition of carte allows such degenerate configurations, but this page does not say so. Morphisms are also left undefined (see the NB).
'Orientable ⇔ such a partition exists' should be stated per connected component. An orientation is a choice of partition on each component.

ideas.what: Duality of maps realized on the same flag set by exchanging the type-0 and type-∞ roles, with reversal of the induced orientations
ideas.modern_name: Dual map; the outer automorphism of the cartographic group / triangle group swapping τ_0 and τ_∞
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Euler/Poincaré duality); in flag/group form Tutte, Jones–Singerman (1978)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the action of S_3 / outer automorphisms on dessins (unsure on detail)

ideas.what: Orientation of a map as a splitting of the flags into two classes exchanged by the reflections and preserved by the rotations
ideas.modern_name: Orientable map; the even-word subgroup G_2^+ of index 2 in the cartographic group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones–Singerman 1978; standard in combinatorial map theory
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §2, cartographic groups C_2 and C_2^+

ideas.what: Equivalence between oriented maps and finite G_2^+-sets, with G_2^+ ≅ Z/2 * Z
ideas.modern_name: Correspondence between oriented maps and permutation representations of the oriented cartographic group (hypermap / dessin correspondence)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard exposition of map duality, orientation via a flag partition, and the equivalence of oriented maps with finite G_2^+-sets. All of this appears in Esquisse d'un programme and in Jones–Singerman. The only intriguing hint, a 'non-trivial' notion of morphism of maps, is not developed on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: '(de grand...)' is likely '(défini combinatoirement)' or similar; 'deviennent ... et inversement' is probably 'deviennent ... et inversement les faces de C correspondent aux sommets de Č'.
The equation label for R(X)=R^+(X)⊔R^-(X) appears to be (6), not (5); (5) was used on the previous page for the ρ_i.
In (7) the intended content is σ_i(R^+(X))=R^-(X), σ_i(R^-(X))=R^+(X), although the manuscript may itself show R^+ / R^-.
(7 bis): the letters read as 'fi' in the image are ρ_i.
'G_2^+-ens. à opérateurs' should read G_2^+-ensemble; in (8) the target is 'G_2^+-ens. finis', and the superscript should be + rather than 0.
The source of (8) is 'Cartes orient.' (the trailing 'or.' is uncertain).
Final NB: 'une notion de "morphisme" de cartes qui n'est pas tellement triviale'; the parenthetical ending is illegible.
